newsitem.title: GERMANY: ABN not eyeing banks in Germany or France.
newsitem.headline: ABN not eyeing banks in Germany or France.

text.p: The chief executive of ABN Amro Holding NV said the Dutch bank saw no acquisition targets in Germany, France or Belgium that would satisfy its earnings requirements.
"Finding a second European home market turned out to be an unrealisable desire," Jan Kalff was quoted as telling German business daily Handelsblatt in an interview published on Tuesday.
"In Germany, France and Belgium there are no banks to buy which could reach our target return within three years."
But Kalff said virtually no bank had a European network that was as dense as ABN Amro's.
He also denied reports that ABN Amro was planning to acquire a U.S. investment bank. In the area of investment banking a purchase entailed a very high risk, he said, adding: "I won't take it."
The bank would only consider purchases on a smaller scale, he said.

Kalff said that that in the long term he expected foreign earnings to exceed domestic income as a proportion of profits and to rise towards 60 percent. The foreign portion of earnings reached 48 percent in the first half of 48 percent.
